verses.text: God's Spirit came upon Azariah son of Oded.

He went out to meet Asa and said, "Listen to me, Asa and everyone in Judah and Benjamin! The LORD is with you as long as you stay with him. If you seek him, you'll find him. If you abandon him, he'll abandon you.
For a long time Israel lived without the true God, without a priest to teach them, and without the law.
But when trouble came, they turned to the LORD, the God of Israel, and sought him, and they found him.
In those days it wasn't safe to come or go. Everyone in the surrounding lands faced serious trouble.
Nation fought nation and town fought town, tearing one another apart, because God troubled them with hardships of every kind.
But you, stay strong and keep working, because your work will be rewarded."

When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage. He removed the detestable idols from Judah, Benjamin, and the towns he'd captured in the hill country of Ephraim. He restored the LORD's altar in front of the temple porch.

Then he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, along with the people from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who were living among them. Many had come to him from Israel because they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
They gathered in Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.
That day they sacrificed to the LORD seven hundred cattle and seven thousand sheep from the plunder they'd brought back.
They made a covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their ancestors, with all their heart and all their soul.
Anyone who refused to seek the LORD, the God of Israel, was to be put to death, regardless of rank or whether they were a man or a woman.
They pledged themselves to the LORD out loud, with shouting and the sound of trumpets and horns.
All Judah celebrated the oath because they'd sworn it wholeheartedly and sought the LORD with everything they had. They found him, and the LORD gave them peace on every side.
King Asa also removed his mother Maacah from her position as queen mother because she'd made a detestable image for Asherah. He cut it down, ground it to dust, and burned it by the Kidron Brook.
The high places remained in Israel, but Asa stayed wholeheartedly devoted all his life.
He brought into God's house the silver, gold, and vessels that he and his father had dedicated.
There was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.
